The distinction between concept and presentation views is immediately legible, which is exactly the point of this exercise. ⚠️ Where to Pivot: The primary weakness is in the bottom-left concept view, where the construction scaffolding near the central ridge becomes so dense that the intended form momentarily loses legibility — the exploratory strokes begin to compete with rather than support the emerging contour. Additionally, the two viewpoints, while technically distinct in elevation angle, are both relatively close in azimuth (both read as roughly three-quarter views from the same side). A more dramatic viewpoint contrast — such as a true top-down plan view paired with a low worm's-eye view — would more powerfully demonstrate the three-dimensionality of the undulating surface.

🛠️ Next Step: Take the same object and produce a single new concept-to-presentation pair from a true top-down (plan) viewpoint. This will force you to represent the undulating surface purely through contour lines and elliptical cross-sections without the aid of perspective foreshortening — a much harder and more revealing test of whether you truly understand the three-dimensional logic of your own form.
